title: Creativity when stuck: search, check, and learn from lucky hits

brief.state:
Creative mode (when B2 is stuck, try many programs, keep the ones a checker accepts, sleep on them) has one tested first climb on DEV and no sealed result yet. Scope is fixed: creativity only for stuck problems (Ben, 10-05 and 10-07); gifts and plans are out. Nothing here touches the village model.

Walls, shown: cold start (P0, 10-06: on 3 unseen kinds, 32 tries by B2 found 1 answer in 240 question-trials across 2 seeds); sameness (2.1-4.5 distinct result-changing programs per question on P0; 4.4 on C1 against 18.7 for a value-blind follower); no checker for open worlds; B2's language cannot write dates or string edits.

C1 (number puzzles with a target checker) was retired at its DEV gate on 10-06. Sleeping on checked right tries lifted plain luck 1.29x on s100 (bar 1.6x) and 1.66x on s101. T1 and T1b were never read.

C2 (rules from a few examples, checked against the prompt's own examples, no answer key) is the main test. Warm-up alone reaches reach@32 of 3.9% and 6.3% (floor 4.8%). Stepping stones written by us reach 25.4% and 19.5% (gate 14.5%), but only at sampling temperatures 2.0-3.0. The C2b DEV pilot (2 parents, 256 questions) gained +34.8 and +27.0 points of greedy first try over the stones parent, all from square and last_digit; affine, sq_plus and double_add stayed near zero and a second night did not climb. Replaying the add/mult rows kept that skill (95%) but gave no climb (+0.6 and +3.2 multi-step). Job 8 gave 480 extra tries to questions with no fitting try and got the first climb on DEV: multi-step first try +10.4 [5.2, 15.6] and +9.7 [5.2, 14.9]; the +10 mark was missed on s101 by one question. Blind search with no model reaches 64.5%, 77.3% and 94.9% at 1k, 6k and 50k candidates on the same kinds, so C2 can only test whether sleep turns search into first answers, not whether it finds answers.

Job 9 is the real C2b: six parents (s200-s205), arms W, R, H (M reported), one sealed 512-question test opened once. The roadmap reports it running on Ben's Mac; no job 9 results are in the repo snapshot. Marks: pooled first-try gain over the parent at least +15, and over R at least +10, both intervals above 0.

Notebook (memory) sleep matched weight sleep on a 2-parent screen at 25-32x fewer FLOPs but failed its 6-seed confirm (0.87x). Hand-written parts still run the loop: the example checker, stepping stones, warm-up solver rows, the 32/480-try schedule, DEV-picked temperatures, and the notebook gate. Learned replacements have sealed marks; none is built.

Measure how many distinct candidates the warm-up parent needs before a checked fit, with model order, a grammar-matched uniform order and blind breadth-first all counted the same way, plus a temperature-matched frontier and a no-stones comparison.
distinct.change: Probe only. Unit: a candidate is a value vector over the 3 examples and the query, first seen in this question's search, across every node of every try; ops 1-7 in all arms. Arms: (a) the model's own sampling order at a DEV-fixed temperature; (b) uniform child order over the model's legal choices (NOOP plus ops 1-7, pointers over valid slots); (c) blind breadth-first read at 32, 128, 512, 1,000 candidates; stop each question at its first fit, 2,000-sample cap reported as a censor. distinct.summary: Several proposed tool replies ('seen before', 'step repeats slot j', residuals) only help if B2's tries actually have those problems. Count them on one logged run first: the share of repeated value vectors, in-cone duplicate steps, failing tries one step from a fit, and late novelty. Blind search predicts the near-miss counts are tiny.
distinct.change: On the stop-rule log (32 plain tries per DEV question at T 1.4 and 3.0, plus 512 on 64 stuck questions): M1 share of calls repeating an earlier value vector on the question's inputs; M2 share of programs with an answer-cone step whose value vector equals an earlier slot's; M3 share of failing calls (structure ok, runs, not fitting) one appended step (ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV using a value the try already has or a constant) from a fit, and share with a constant offset; M5 share of stuck questions still producing new value patterns after call 256. Replies are built only if their counter passes.
distinct.why: Shown on blind search: only 0.34% of failing affine candidates are one step from a fit (0.03% with a constant operand) and 0.22% have a constant offset; sq_plus 0.34% and 0.71%. The step-cap motivation for the duplicate-step reply is refuted: the three 'not representable' affine pairs fit in 5-6 steps and all usable pairs need at most 5. B2's own rates are untested.

distinct.title: Temperature-free diversity: first-step branching and output-vector dedupe
distinct.summary: Replace heat with two sampling rules at T=1: split the draws over the model's own top-8 first steps, and keep a try only if its outputs on the question's visible inputs are new. A zero-training probe first asks whether each held-out kind's reference first step even sits in the top 8, and whether the model's tries cover several affine classes.
distinct.change: New sampling paths in creative/sampler.py and legal.py. Probe P0: for each DEV question, is the reference first step (R.reference remapped as in fewshot.pc_records, commutative operands sorted) in first_step_candidates' top 8? Arm B1: 4 tries per top-8 first step at T=1, every draw counted toward the 32. Arm D: one try at a time at T=1, keep only if the output vector on the example x values plus the query x is new, stop at 32 kept or 128 draws, all draws counted. Census (w1c-5): distinct affine classes (A,B) hit per question among 32 tries at T 1.0 and 3.0. Controls: C1 picked-T 32 draws, C2 same T 128 draws, E T=1 128 draws with replacement, blind with 32 and 128 candidates.
distinct.why: Shown: stone-parent reach@32 at T 1.0 is 7.8%/7.4% against 25.4%/19.5% at T 3.0; square 0.02/0.04 against 0.82/0.71; distinct rule-following programs 7.9/7.6 at T 1.0 against 14.4/15.7 at T 3.0. C2b has no branching and no dedup; first-step branching kept about 7 result-changing programs per puzzle near T=0 on C1 only. Note: dedupe at equal draws leaves the set of patterns unchanged for independent draws; the gain exists only through the draw cap (128 draws) or a model that conditions on repeats.

distinct.title: Depth-bounded exact closure as the only honest 'cannot'
distinct.summary: A cannot that is not a guess can come from an exact, key-free closure over the example outputs: the set of output vectors reachable within d steps. Extra certificate with no search: the same input given two different outputs means no function of x fits at any depth. Every cannot output names its depth.

distinct.title: Record purity and pick audit before any selection rule
distinct.summary: Several proposals assume that which checked fit you keep matters (vote, shortest, likelihood, first, functional key). On C2 blind search the first fit is right almost always, so the premise may be closed; on search-hard kinds it is not. Measure key-right share of accepted tries, contradictory answers, functional duplicates and false accepts at 3 versus 5 examples, then build a sleep arm only if the audit opens the question.
distinct.change: Audit on the stop-rule log (and the panel): (i) key-right share of accepted tries per kind and T; (ii) share of questions with two or more distinct query answers among their fits (contradictory targets); (iii) functional duplicates among expression-distinct pairs, using output signature on the prompt numbers and x-1, x+1, 2x; (iv) pickers: first, random, plurality vote of query answers, shortest, own log-likelihood (untempered, forced path), pinned (all fits agree) versus open; (v) false-accept share over all fitting programs at 3 versus 5 examples (blind search to 50,000 candidates, k_ex 3 versus 5). Sleep arms (vote-two, functional-key cap, majority filter, first-two) run only if key-right is under 90% on two or more parents.
distinct.why: Shown: on C2 DEV blind first fit is right on 189 of 191 questions with a fit and plurality equals it; on multi-step the first fit is right on every one of 89 questions with a fit. B2's accepted precision at T 3.0 is 93.9-100% (about 15 wrong of 302 samples, DEV, stone arms only; job-8 W records unmeasured). But on panel-style kinds blind pinned questions are right 73% versus 30% for open ones, own-likelihood headroom is 17 of 90 tier-1 questions, and capped/rounded-up kinds gave 4 of 4 wrong fits with 3 examples.
